liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (4 reviews): The late show features one of the last Dark Stars with Tom Constanten, sounding like Seastones; The jam begins with ten minutes of alien silence before emerging into one of their hottest performances [8][13][14][15]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Lovelight especially rages, providing a strong finish despite a cut in St. Stephen; Pigpen and Bobby are on, working together to close the show with a bang [15][16]
- **Mason's Children** (1 review): This performance matches the brilliant version found on the Fallout from the Phil zone release [5]
- **High Time** (1 review): High Time is very well executed, likely the reviewer's favorite version of the song [14]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): The transition into St. Stephen is described as the funkiest version they ever played [13]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): The Eleven is described as a powerhouse performance, while Lovelight provides a perfect rave-up ending [6]

## The recordings

- **gd70-01-02.early-late.sbd.cotsman.18120.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 182 min; rated 4.21/5 by 46 [1]
- **gd1970-01-02.137375.sbd.wise.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 180 min; rated 3.33/5 by 9 [2]
- **gd70-01-02.late.sbd.hanno.12624.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 71 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [3]
- **gd70-01-02.partial-early.sbd.86.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 35 min; rated 4.5/5 by 22 [4]. Said about its sound: The recording quality is superb, with Dark Star featuring unique layering from the 19-minute mark; Cymbals, maracas, and snare drum are right up front in this astounding recording quality; Hiss from the original tape is present, making it a sick recording to listen to with lights out [6][7][12]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Zarathustra [1]
- Reviewer questions if Tom Constanten and Micky Hart were with the band, comparing organ styles [7]
- Band walked on stage to 2001 theme, purple screen background, and white block letters [18]
- The file labeled late is actually the Early show, according to deadlists.com evidence [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-01-02.early-late.sbd.cotsman.18120.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Thanks to A. Lemiex, Uli, and Hanno for the early and late show matrix [1]
- **gd1970-01-02.137375.sbd.wise.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by SIRMick; source: Soundboard > 7 1/2' Reel Master @ 7.5 ips (Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel Deck) > 1st gen (TDK SAX-100 cassette) from Dick Latvala (Master Reel Playback… [2]. Also: Setlist relabeled Early in 2001 based on witness account, but later evidence supports Late show [2]
- **gd70-01-02.late.sbd.hanno.12624.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: SBD plus AUD patches, sourced via Hanno Bunjes and Uli Teute for the late show [3]
- **gd70-01-02.partial-early.sbd.86.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Stephen Windsor; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: SBD to MR to DAT to CDR to EAC, via S. Windsor and D. Sacks [4]
